headline: Highest risk is medium: mem0 can ingest content while Pathway is a local-only, no-write processor, so prompt-injection and leakage are limited but not impossible in shared-workspace setups.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: mem0 is a knowledge-management agent that may ingest and later surface content, while Pathway is a document-processing pipeline with no clipboard/MCP/browser surfaces. No shared channel is documented, so direct hijack is not shown; the remaining pathway is unusual copy/paste or file handoff, which keeps blast radius small.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies Pathway output into mem0 prompts or memory entries
IF a shared file or workspace is introduced outside the documented profiles
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Avoid copy-pasting untrusted Pathway output into mem0
Add a human review step before mem0 ingests generated text
Use explicit delimiters for any transferred content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents are docs-only and show no filesystem read/write or network egress, so there is no documented automatic exfiltration path. A leakage pathway only appears if the operator places sensitive files into a shared workspace or manually transfers them between the agents, making the blast radius limited.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are manually placed into a shared directory
IF mem0 is configured to store user content from Pathway outputs
mitigations: Do not co-locate sensitive files
Use separate service accounts and directories
Redact secrets before transfer
Disable any optional persistence of transferred content

C_capability_conflict.rationale: mem0 exposes no write or git capabilities in the profile, and Pathway explicitly cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. With no overlapping mutable surface, a capability conflict pathway is provably blocked by the profiles.
conditions: IF either profile is extended with shared write access to the same directory
mitigations: Keep Pathway read-only
Do not grant mem0 filesystem write access
Avoid shared git repositories
Reassess if either agent gains mutable resource access

D_cascading_error.rationale: mem0 can preserve and re-surface content, and Pathway is a document-processing system that may feed outputs downstream. If Pathway output is treated as authoritative by mem0 without verification, errors can cascade across work products even though neither profile shows direct action-taking authority.
conditions: IF Pathway outputs are ingested into mem0 as trusted facts
IF no verification or provenance check is inserted before reuse
mitigations: Require source citations on transferred facts
Insert a verification step before mem0 stores Pathway output
Tag generated content as untrusted
Limit mem0 to retrieval, not automatic action

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes, residency constraints, or retention policies are documented for either agent, and both profiles show docs-only evidence with no PHI/PII handling. Because the compliance pathway is not evidenced, there is no specific mismatch to score.
conditions: IF either agent is later configured to process regulated data classes
mitigations: Document data-class handling
Review residency and retention settings
Add a DPA or equivalent if regulated data is introduced
Reassess compliance before deployment
